change: Third review round and its verification, the study tool and the procedure (procedure 0.7.0), in two rounds. First round: the lock binds every file a command names, read from the study directory, and everything Python could import beside them; the plan check requires the subject (pair), a dated window and four required criteria, and refuses unknown keys, a key given twice and more than one opening; a test case is two parts, the data and what was put in, and the method is given the data alone; the record of what has been opened is matched by log fingerprint; a verdict counts only after the finding, the signature names the finding by checksum, and the log check applies the locked rules to the run receipt again; the system trial's verdict is written to the study log; the lock binds the request and records the procedure's checksum; the scorecard check clean-opening is renamed no-failed-opening and lock-committed is added. Second round, after an independent verifier: every command in a plan is a launcher the tool knows ({python}, or uv run) followed by a script file that exists and is bound, and anything else is refused by the plan check; a rehearsal lists the files it needs under needs, which the tool looks for itself and the lock binds; commands and git run in an environment built from a short list of names, with further names only where a plan step lists them under passes_environment, and each run records the names it was given; power_to_refute_when_false can no longer be waived; the known-answer tests run the method in a process of its own that is given only the data, in shuffled batches, and keep what was put in, the seed and the scoring to themselves; the self-test check on an opening whose fetch exited 0 now exercises its guard, and four other checks that could pass for another reason were tightened.
predicted: The known-answer numbers for this study do not move for the same seeds: coverage 0.9325, minimum over hard cases 0.9238, false confirmation right at the difference that matters 0.0395, false refutation there 0.0385, supported when true 0.9465, refuted when false 0.9715. The method without the quality screen still fails the known-answer tests and with the screen passes. The blind test of 200 cases gives the same result as before both rounds: of 100 cases where the idea is true, 82 supported and 18 inconclusive; of 100 where it is false, 94 refuted and 6 inconclusive; none wrong. The known-answer tests take longer, because every case now crosses a process boundary: between a quarter and a half longer than the minute they took. (A run in a scratch copy while the change was being made had already given these numbers; this record is made before any test of this practice run.)

rationale: First round: three reviewers reached the status ready for the steward's signature with a doctored receipt, with code changed after the lock, with the held-out data opened twice and with an opening voided after it had read its data, and passed the system trial with a method that estimates nothing. Second round: the verifier ran the locked analysis from inside a shell string, swapped it after the lock and got a supported result with a log check that reported no problem; read the value put in off the known-answer harness's call stack from inside the method and passed every criterion with a method that estimates nothing; waived the one criterion that shows a rule can refute; and found a self-test check that still passed with its guard removed. The method's inputs change in one way only (a test case no longer carries what was put in, and the method never read it) and its arithmetic is untouched: it now runs in another process on the same data, so no number should move.
